subject: Visualising the results for estimated ELPD and its standard error

messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Visualising the results for estimated ELPD and its standard error
parts:
Hi,

I want to show the results for estimated ELPD across a number of models, which has been estimated using K-fold cross validation on a hierarchical model. 

I have used the method in Vehtari et al. (2015) 'Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC', to estimate the ELPD, and its standard error across a number of models. I would now like to make a graph of these results for a publication. However, I realise that really this measure is meant only to be used for pairwise comparisons; if model A's ELPD is higher than model B's, accounting for the standard error of their difference, then we prefer the former.

As such, does it make sense to graph these results at all? The issue I am having is illustrated in the attached pdf. This shows the point estimates of the ELPD for each of 7 models, along with the standard errors. When viewed this way, it looks like I shouldn't prefer the exponential model over the gompertz-Makeham one, since there is considerably overlap in their standard errors. 

However, when I explicitly estimate the standard error of their difference, as:

se = sqrt(N sum_i var(lpd_i^exponential - lpd_i^gompertz-makeham)

I find that there is a difference between them in terms of score. As such, I am unclear whether it makes any sense to graph these results at all, and perhaps I just need to mention this in the text. Does a graph of these model scores make any sense, or should I just shelve it?

If there are other ways to visualise these scores, that I have not considered, then also it'd be good to hear them!

Best,

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Visualising the results for estimated ELPD and its standard error
parts:
I think the graph is almost fine — you just need to select one of the models as the
“default” and plot everything relative to the nominal estimate of that model’s ELPD.
Then everything is readily interpreted as pairwise comparisons.

Personally in these circumstances I like showing a grey band in the background
for the standard errors on the nominal model so that by eye you can estimate the
significance of the difference based on the overlap between the grey band and
the interval of each particular model.  But that might not be a universally well-liked
visualization.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Visualising the results for estimated ELPD and its standard error
parts:
But the se’s can be pretty useless as is, as is indicated by the way in which comparisons between models can be much more precise than what you’d expect based on the calculation sqrt(se_1^2+se_2^2).  Reminds me that we have to write the paper with 2-way Anova for loo/waic comparisons.
A
